greek: Ταῦτα τὰ ὀνόματα τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ τῶν εἰσπεπορευμένων εἰς Αἴγυπτον ἅμα Ιακωβ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτῶν — ἕκαστος πανοικίᾳ αὐτῶν εἰσήλθοσαν —·
hint: The names of Israel's sons who went into Egypt with Jacob, each with his household.

notes.text: With Jacob their father: the Hebrew has ʾēt yaʿăqōb, with Jacob, without their father.
Perfect participle of εἰσπορεύομαι: the ones who have entered, and are there.

Not in Middle Liddell; LSJ gives πανοικία, whole household, and the dative as an adverb, with all the house, the dative's own English and so not marked again. The nominative of GEN 50:8 has the first alone.

reading: [[these|these, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] [[the names|the names, the fames, the mere names, the phrases and expressions|ὄνομα]] of the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[of the ones having gone into|of the ones having gone into and entered and standing so|εἰσπορεύομαι]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in|εἰς]] [[name:Αἴγυπτον]] [[at the same time with|at the same time with and together with, at once and the same time|ἅμα]] to [[name:Ιακωβ]] [[to the father|to the father, to the grandfather|πατήρ]] of them — [[every|every, every one, each, each one, all and each one, singly and by itself, each by himself|ἕκαστος]] [[to whole household|to whole household, with all the house|πανοικία]] of them [[went in|went in, went into and entered, came into, came in, came upon|εἰσέρχομαι]] —;

names.gloss: (Ισραηλ, from Hebrew Yiśrāʾēl, which the Hebrew of Genesis 32:29 hears in śārâ ʿim ʾĕlōhîm, "he strove with God")
(Αἴγυπτος, the Greek name of the land; Hebrew Miṣrayim)
(Ιακωβ, from Hebrew Yaʿăqōb, which the Hebrew of Genesis 25:26 hears in ʿāqēb, "heel")

greek: Ρουβην, Συμεων, Λευι, Ιουδας,
hint: The list of Jacob's sons begins: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah.

notes.text: Leah's first four sons, in the order of their births at Genesis 29:32–35.

reading: [[name:Ρουβην]], [[name:Συμεων]], [[name:Λευι]], [[name:Ιουδας]],

names.gloss: (Ρουβην, from Hebrew Rĕʾûbēn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:32 hears in rāʾâ bĕʿonyî, "he has seen my affliction")
(Συμεων, from Hebrew Šimʿôn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:33 hears in šāmaʿ, "he heard")
(Λευι, from Hebrew Lēwî, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:34 hears in lāwâ, "he was joined")
(Ιουδας, from Hebrew Yĕhûdâ, which the Hebrew of Genesis 29:35 hears in yādâ, "to praise")

greek: Ισσαχαρ, Ζαβουλων καὶ Βενιαμιν,
hint: The list goes on with Issachar, Zebulun and Benjamin.

notes.text: Leah's last two sons, then Rachel's younger; Joseph, her elder, is named apart in 1:5.

reading: [[name:Ισσαχαρ]], [[name:Ζαβουλων]] and [[name:Βενιαμιν]],

names.gloss: (Ισσαχαρ, from Hebrew Yiśśāśkār, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:18 hears in śākār, "wages")
(Ζαβουλων, from Hebrew Zĕbûlûn, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:20 hears in zābal, "to dwell with honour")
(Βενιαμιν, from Hebrew Binyāmîn, "son of the right hand" or "son of the south")

greek: Δαν καὶ Νεφθαλι, Γαδ καὶ Ασηρ.
hint: The list ends with the four sons of the maidservants: Dan, Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

notes.text: Bilhah's sons, then Zilpah's, as at Genesis 35:25–26.

reading: [[name:Δαν]] and [[name:Νεφθαλι]], [[name:Γαδ]] and [[name:Ασηρ]].

names.gloss: (Δαν, from Hebrew Dān, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:6 hears in dîn, "he judged")
(Νεφθαλι, from Hebrew Naptālî, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:8 hears in niptal, "I have wrestled")
(Γαδ, from Hebrew Gād, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:11 hears in gād, "fortune")
(Ασηρ, from Hebrew ʾĀšēr, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:13 hears in ʾōšer, "happiness")

greek: Ιωσηφ δὲ ἦν ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ. ἦσαν δὲ πᾶσαι ψυχαὶ ἐξ Ιακωβ πέντε καὶ ἑβδομήκοντα.
hint: Joseph was already in Egypt; Jacob's descendants number seventy-five, where the Hebrew counts seventy.

notes.text: Seventy-five, as at Genesis 46:27 in this Greek; the Hebrew has šibʿîm, seventy. Stephen's speech, Acts 7:14, gives seventy-five.
The Greek puts Joseph first; the Hebrew counts the souls first and ends with Joseph.
From Jacob: the Hebrew has yōṣĕʾê yerek yaʿăqōb, coming out of Jacob's thigh.

reading: [[name:Ιωσηφ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to [[name:Αἰγύπτῳ]]. were, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[all|all, the whole, every, every single|πᾶς]] [[breaths|breaths, lives, spirits, life and death, ghosts, departed souls|ψυχή]] [[out of|out of, forth from, from|ἐκ]] of [[name:Ιακωβ]] five and seventy.

names.gloss: (Ιωσηφ, from Hebrew Yôsēp̄, which the Hebrew of Genesis 30:24 hears in yōsēp̄, "may he add")

greek: ἐτελεύτησεν δὲ Ιωσηφ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἀδελφοὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πᾶσα ἡ γενεὰ ἐκείνη.
hint: Joseph dies, and all his brothers, and that whole generation.

notes.text: τελευτάω, to complete, to finish, and of life, to end it: one singular verb for all three subjects.

greek: οἱ δὲ υἱοὶ Ισραηλ ηὐξήθησαν καὶ ἐπληθύνθησαν καὶ χυδαῖοι ἐγένοντο καὶ κατίσχυον σφόδρα σφόδρα, ἐπλήθυνεν δὲ ἡ γῆ αὐτούς.
hint: The sons of Israel grow and multiply beyond measure, and the land is filled with them.

notes.text: They became abundant, χυδαῖος, poured out in streams: LSJ cites this verse. The Hebrew has wayyišrĕṣû, they swarmed.
The land was multiplying them, active with the land as subject; the Hebrew has wattimmālēʾ hāʾāreṣ ʾōtām, the land was filled with them.
Imperfect or aorist, one spelling in the third singular; read with the imperfect κατίσχυον before it.

reading: [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[were made large|were made large and increased and augmented, were increased in power and strengthened and exalted and aggrandised, were promoted to honour and glorified and magnified, grew and waxed and increased, grew up|αὐξάνω]] and [[were made full|were made full and increased and multiplied, were in the majority and prevailed|πληθύνω]] and [[poured out in streams|poured out in streams and abundant, common and ordinary, common and vulgar and coarse|χυδαῖος]] [[came into being|came to be, arose, were brought into existence|γίνομαι]] and [[were having power over|were having power over and overpowering and prevailing against, were coming to their full strength|κατισχύω]] [[very|very and very much and exceedingly and violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]] [[very|very and very much and exceedingly and violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]], [[was making full|was making full and increasing and multiplying|πληθύνω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] them.

greek: Ἀνέστη δὲ βασιλεὺς ἕτερος ἐπʼ Αἴγυπτον, ὃς οὐκ ᾔδει τὸν Ιωσηφ.
hint: A new king arises over Egypt who did not know Joseph.

notes.text: Pluperfect of οἶδα, whose perfect is a present: he knew.
ἕτερος, other, one of two: the Hebrew has ḥādāš, new.

reading: [[stood up|stood up, rose, rose to fight against, rose to go and set out|ἀνίστημι]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[a king|a king and chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] [[other|other, one of two, the other of two, another, second, different, other than, worse|ἕτερος]] [[upon|upon, on, in, at, near|ἐπί + accusative]] [[name:Αἴγυπτον]], who not [[knew|knew, was assured, was versed in|οἶδα]] the [[name:Ιωσηφ]].

greek: εἶπεν δὲ τῷ ἔθνει αὐτοῦ Ἰδοὺ τὸ γένος τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ μέγα πλῆθος καὶ ἰσχύει ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς·
hint: The king tells his people that the race of Israel's sons is a great multitude, stronger than they are.

notes.lemma: μέγα πλῆθος καὶ ἰσχύει ὑπὲρ ἡμᾶς
notes.text: A great multitude, and strong beyond us: the Hebrew has rab wĕʿāṣûm mimmennû, many and mightier than we.

greek: δεῦτε οὖν κατασοφισώμεθα αὐτούς, μήποτε πληθυνθῇ καί, ἡνίκα ἂν συμβῇ ἡμῖν πόλεμος, προστεθήσονται καὶ οὗτοι πρὸς τοὺς ὑπεναντίους καὶ ἐκπολεμήσαντες ἡμᾶς ἐξελεύσονται ἐκ τῆς γῆς.
hint: He proposes outwitting them, in case they multiply and join an enemy in war and leave the land.

notes.text: κατασοφίζομαι, to get the better of by sophistry, to outwit: the Hebrew nitḥakkĕmâ, let us deal wisely. Acts 7:19 takes the same verb for the king's dealing.
Having made war on us, or roused us to war: the Hebrew has wĕnilḥam-bānû, and fight against us.

greek: καὶ ἐπέστησεν αὐτοῖς ἐπιστάτας τῶν ἔργων, ἵνα κακώσωσιν αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις· καὶ ᾠκοδόμησαν πόλεις ὀχυρὰς τῷ Φαραω, τήν τε Πιθωμ καὶ Ραμεσση καὶ Ων, ἥ ἐστιν Ἡλίου πόλις.
hint: Egypt sets overseers on them, and they build fortified cities for Pharaoh: Pithom, Rameses, and On, that is Heliopolis.

notes.lemma: καὶ Ων, ἥ ἐστιν Ἡλίου πόλις
notes.text: And On, which is Heliopolis: not in the Hebrew, which names Pithom and Raamses only.
Strong cities: the Hebrew has ʿārê miskĕnôt, store cities.
Overseers of the works, for the Hebrew śārê missîm, chiefs of forced labour.
First aorist of ἐφίστημι, the causal tense: he set over.

names.gloss: (Φαραω, from Hebrew Parʿōh, from the Egyptian for "great house")
(Πιθωμ, from Hebrew Pitōm, from the Egyptian Per-Atum, "house of Atum")
(Ραμεσση, from Hebrew Raʿamsēs, the Egyptian royal name Ramesses)
(Ων, from Hebrew ʾÔn, the Egyptian city the Greek names Ἡλίου πόλις)
(Ἥλιος, the sun; Ἡλίου πόλις, the city of the sun, the Greek name of the Egyptian city Hebrew calls ʾÔn)

greek: καθότι δὲ αὐτοὺς ἐταπείνουν, τοσούτῳ πλείους ἐγίνοντο καὶ ἴσχυον σφόδρα σφόδρα· καὶ ἐβδελύσσοντο οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν Ισραηλ.
hint: The more the Egyptians oppress them, the more they multiply, and the Egyptians come to loathe them.

notes.text: In what measure … by so much: τοσοῦτος in the dative with a comparative, the measure of the difference.
And they grew very very strong: not in the Hebrew, which has kēn yirbeh wĕkēn yip̄rōṣ, so they multiplied and so they spread.
βδελύσσομαι, to feel nausea, to loathe: for the Hebrew wayyāquṣû, they felt dread.

names.gloss: (Αἰγύπτιος, the man of Αἴγυπτος, Egypt)

greek: καὶ κατεδυνάστευον οἱ Αἰγύπτιοι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ισραηλ βίᾳ
hint: The Egyptians lord it over the sons of Israel by force.

notes.text: καταδυναστεύω, Middle Liddell's one translation, to exercise power over: plain text. The Hebrew has wayyaʿăbidû, they made them serve.
By force, the dative used as an adverb, perforce: the Hebrew has bĕp̄ārek, with harshness.

reading: and were exercising power over the [[name:Αἰγύπτιοι]] the sons of [[name:Ισραηλ]] [[to bodily strength|to bodily strength and force and power and might, to force and an act of violence, against one's will and in spite of, perforce|βία]]

greek: καὶ κατωδύνων αὐτῶν τὴν ζωὴν ἐν τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς σκληροῖς, τῷ πηλῷ καὶ τῇ πλινθείᾳ καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ἔργοις τοῖς ἐν τοῖς πεδίοις, κατὰ πάντα τὰ ἔργα, ὧν κατεδουλοῦντο αὐτοὺς μετὰ βίας.
hint: They make the Israelites' life bitter with hard work in clay and brickmaking and all the field labour.

notes.text: κατοδυνάω, to afflict grievously: not in Middle Liddell; LSJ cites this verse for its one translation, plain text. The Hebrew has wayĕmārărû, they made bitter.
In clay and in brickmaking: the Hebrew has bĕḥōmer ûbilbēnîm, in mortar and in bricks.
In the plains, for the Hebrew baśśādeh, in the field.

greek: Καὶ εἶπεν ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Αἰγυπτίων ταῖς μαίαις τῶν Εβραίων, τῇ μιᾷ αὐτῶν, ᾗ ὄνομα Σεπφωρα, καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τῆς δευτέρας Φουα,
hint: The king of Egypt speaks to the Hebrews' midwives, Shiphrah and Puah.

notes.text: The midwives of the Hebrews: the genitive leaves open whether they were Hebrew themselves, as the Hebrew hamĕyalĕdōt hāʿibriyyōt does.
Middle Liddell's first sense is good mother, dame, a term of address for an old woman; midwife is its last.

reading: and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] [[the king|the king and chief, the hereditary king, the lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of the [[name:Αἰγυπτίων]] [[to the good mothers|to the good mothers and dames, to the fostermothers and nurses, to the true mothers, to the midwives|μαῖα]] of the [[name:Εβραίων]], [[to the one|to the one, to a single one and one alone|εἷς]] of them, to which [[a name|a name, fame, a mere name, a phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[name:Σεπφωρα]], and [[the name|the name, the fame, the mere name, the phrase and expression|ὄνομα]] [[of the second|of the second, of the one coming in second, of the next best, of the next, of the one after, of the secondly and next and afterwards and a second time, of the second time, of the secondary, of the second of two|δεύτερος]] [[name:Φουα]],

names.gloss: (Εβραῖος, from Hebrew ʿIbrî, usually connected with ʿēber, "the region beyond")
(Σεπφωρα, from Hebrew Šiprâ, usually connected with šāpar, "to be fair")
(Φουα, from Hebrew Pûʿâ, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ εἶπεν Ὅταν μαιοῦσθε τὰς Εβραίας καὶ ὦσιν πρὸς τῷ τίκτειν, ἐὰν μὲν ἄρσεν ᾖ, ἀποκτείνατε αὐτό, ἐὰν δὲ θῆλυ, περιποιεῖσθε αὐτό.
hint: He orders them to kill the Hebrew women's sons at birth and let the daughters live.

notes.text: And they are near the bearing: the Hebrew has ûrĕʾîten ʿal-hāʾobnāyim, and you look upon the birth-stones.
μαιόομαι, to deliver: Middle Liddell's one translation, plain text. Subjunctive after ὅταν, spelled as the indicative, as Koine spells the subjunctive of -όω verbs.
Present middle of περιποιέω: keep for yourselves, preserve. The Hebrew has wāḥāyâ, she shall live.

greek: ἐφοβήθησαν δὲ αἱ μαῖαι τὸν θεὸν καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησαν καθότι συνέταξεν αὐταῖς ὁ βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἐζωογόνουν τὰ ἄρσενα.
hint: The midwives fear God and do not obey the king, but keep the male children alive.

notes.text: ζωογονέω, to engender life, and as ζωγρέω, to keep alive: not in Middle Liddell; LSJ cites this verse for to preserve alive.

greek: ἐκάλεσεν δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς Αἰγύπτου τὰς μαίας καὶ εἶπεν αὐταῖς Τί ὅτι ἐποιήσατε τὸ πρᾶγμα τοῦτο καὶ ἐζωογονεῖτε τὰ ἄρσενα;
hint: The king calls the midwives and asks why they have done this and let the boys live.

notes.text: Why is it that: τί, the accusative used as an adverb, as at Genesis 18:13.

reading: [[called|called, summoned, called to himself, invited|καλέω]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[the king|the king and chief, the hereditary king, the lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia|βασιλεύς]] of [[name:Αἰγύπτου]] [[the good mothers|the good mothers and dames, the fostermothers and nurses, the true mothers, the midwives|μαῖα]] and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told|λέγω]] to them why [[that|that, seeing that, although, for that, because, inasmuch as|ὅτι]] [[you made|you made, you did, you produced, you created|ποιέω]] [[the that which has been done|the that which has been done and deed and act, the anything necessary and expedient, the thing of consequence and importance, the action and affair, the thing and the business|πρᾶγμα]] [[this|this, the nearer, what follows|οὗτος]] and [[you were propagating|you were propagating, you were engendering living creatures, you were breeding, you were engendering, you were being viviparous, you were producing alive, you were making alive and quickening, you were preserving alive|ζωογονέω]] [[the male|the male, the male sex, the masculine and strong, the mighty|ἄρσην]]?

greek: εἶπαν δὲ αἱ μαῖαι τῷ Φαραω Οὐχ ὡς γυναῖκες Αἰγύπτου αἱ Εβραῖαι, τίκτουσιν γὰρ πρὶν ἢ εἰσελθεῖν πρὸς αὐτὰς τὰς μαίας· καὶ ἔτικτον.
hint: The midwives tell Pharaoh that Hebrew women are not like Egyptian women: they give birth before a midwife arrives.

notes.text: For they bear: the Hebrew first says kî-ḥāyôt hēnnâ, for they are lively, which the Greek has not.
πρὶν ἤ with the infinitive and its subject in the accusative, τὰς μαίας: before the midwives come in.

greek: εὖ δὲ ἐποίει ὁ θεὸς ταῖς μαίαις, καὶ ἐπλήθυνεν ὁ λαὸς καὶ ἴσχυεν σφόδρα.
hint: God deals well with the midwives, and the people grow numerous and very strong.

notes.text: Was doing well to: εὖ ποιέω with the dative, to benefit.

reading: [[well|well, luckily, happily, well off|εὖ]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand|δέ]], [[was making|was making, was doing, was producing, was creating|ποιέω]] [[the God|he who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]] [[to the good mothers|to the good mothers and dames, to the fostermothers and nurses, to the true mothers, to the midwives|μαῖα]], and [[was making full|was making full and increasing and multiplying|πληθύνω]] [[the people|the people, the men, the soldiers, the land-army, the common men, the folk, the Jews, the Christians|λαός]] and [[was being strong|was being strong and mighty and powerful and prevailing, was having power and influence|ἰσχύω]] [[very|very and very much and exceedingly and violently, far, most certainly|σφόδρα]].

greek: ἐπειδὴ ἐφοβοῦντο αἱ μαῖαι τὸν θεόν, ἐποίησαν ἑαυταῖς οἰκίας. —
hint: Because the midwives fear God, they make households for themselves.

notes.text: They made households for themselves: the Hebrew has wayyaʿaś lāhem bāttîm, he made them houses, God the subject.

reading: [[after that|after that, after, since, when, from the time when and ever since, whenever, as soon as, seeing that, for, although, else and otherwise|ἐπειδή]] [[were being put to flight|were being put to flight, were fleeing affrighted, were fleeing, were being seized with fear, were being affrighted, were fearing|φοβέομαι]] [[the good mothers|the good mothers and dames, the fostermothers and nurses, the true mothers, the midwives|μαῖα]] [[the God|him who is God definitively, the one the article marks out, the known and the only|θεός]], [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] to themselves [[buildings|buildings, houses, dwellings, households and domestic establishments, households and inmates of the house, houses and families from which one is descended|οἰκία]]. —

greek: συνέταξεν δὲ Φαραω παντὶ τῷ λαῷ αὐτοῦ λέγων Πᾶν ἄρσεν, ὃ ἐὰν τεχθῇ τοῖς Εβραίοις, εἰς τὸν ποταμὸν ῥίψατε· καὶ πᾶν θῆλυ, ζωογονεῖτε αὐτό.
hint: Pharaoh commands all his people to throw every Hebrew boy into the river and keep every girl alive.

notes.text: To the Hebrews: not in the Hebrew, which has kol-habbēn hayyillôd, every son that is born.
A hanging nominative taken up by αὐτό: every female, keep it alive.
